clues: the new link between the buildings never comes up or drops after a few minutes
the patch cord has a yellow jacket while the transceivers are rated for 850 nm
the same transceivers work with the old orange patch cords
the link light flickers but no traffic passes

answer.cause: a single-mode patch cord used with multimode transceivers
answer.action: Replace the patch cord with multimode fiber that matches the transceivers

firstStep: Check the fiber type printed on the patch cord against the transceiver specs
appliesWhen: the fiber type does not match the optics at its ends
explanation: Short-range 850 nm optics are made for multimode fiber, and a yellow jacket marks single-mode cable. A fiber type mismatch can keep the link down or make it unstable.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the workstation links at 1 Gbps although the switch port and NIC support 10 Gbps
the jacket of the old patch cord is printed Cat 5
a newer patch cord from the stockroom gives the full speed
no errors show on the switch port

answer.cause: a lower-category cable that cannot carry the link speed
answer.action: Replace the cable with Cat 6a or better

firstStep: Read the category printed on the cable jacket
appliesWhen: the cable is rated for a lower speed than the link needs
explanation: Each cable category has a top speed and distance. An old Cat 5 cord cannot carry 10GBASE-T, so the ports fall back to a lower speed.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the drops on the factory floor run past large motors and welders
errors rise whenever the production line starts
the cable is plain Cat 6 with no foil or braid
the same model of cable works well in the office area

answer.cause: unshielded cable installed where a shielded cable is needed
answer.action: Replace the run with shielded twisted pair (STP) or fiber

appliesWhen: a plain unshielded cable runs through an area full of electrical noise
explanation: Unshielded cable has no protection against the strong electrical noise of motors and welders. Shielded twisted pair or fiber resists that noise.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the errors started after new fluorescent light fixtures were installed
the cable lies on top of the light fittings above the ceiling tiles
the cable tests clean when it is laid on the floor
users on that run see slow transfers and retransmissions

answer.cause: electromagnetic interference (EMI) from the light fixtures next to the cable
answer.action: Reroute the cable away from the fixtures, or use shielded cable for that path

firstStep: Look at the path of the cable above the ceiling
appliesWhen: a cable lies next to a source of electrical noise such as lights or power lines
explanation: Fluorescent fixtures, elevators, and power lines make electromagnetic fields that corrupt the signal in copper cable. Running the cable away from them, or shielding it, removes the noise.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the certifier reports a NEXT failure on the run
the pairs are untwisted for several centimeters behind the patch panel
the wire map test shows every pin in the right place
the link works at 100 Mbps but fails at 1 Gbps

answer.cause: near-end crosstalk between pairs left untwisted at the termination
answer.action: Reterminate the run, keeping each pair twisted up to the punch-down point

appliesWhen: the pairs are untwisted too far where the cable is terminated
explanation: The twists cancel the signal that one pair puts on its neighbor. Untwisting too much at the panel lets the pairs couple, which a certifier reports as near-end crosstalk.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the run goes from the closet to a new office at the far end of the warehouse
the measured length is about 140 meters
the link drops in and out and shows many errors
the cable tests with no opens or shorts

answer.cause: attenuation because the copper run is longer than 100 meters
answer.action: Shorten the run by adding a switch or repeater closer to the office, or use fiber

firstStep: Measure the cable length with a TDR or cable certifier
appliesWhen: the copper run is longer than its rated distance
explanation: Signals weaken as they travel, and twisted pair is rated for 100 meters. Past that length the signal is too weak, which causes intermittent errors.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the connection drops when the patch cord is moved
the outer jacket stops short of the plug, so the bare wires show
the conductors do not reach the end of the plug
a different patch cord works without problems

answer.cause: a badly crimped connector on the patch cord
answer.action: Cut off the plug and crimp a new connector, or replace the patch cord

firstStep: Swap in a known-good patch cord
appliesWhen: a plug was crimped badly, so the pins make poor contact
explanation: When the wires do not reach the pins and the jacket is not held by the plug, contact is poor and changes when the cord moves. Proper termination fixes the contact.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the wall jack stopped working after workers installed new shelving
a cable tester shows no continuity on two pairs
the patch cords at both ends test good
the port shows no link at all

answer.cause: a cable in the wall cut or crushed during the work
answer.action: Repair or replace the damaged run in the wall

firstStep: Test the in-wall run with a cable tester
appliesWhen: the in-wall cable has a break or a short
explanation: Losing continuity on pairs inside the wall right after building work points to a cut or crushed run. An open breaks the circuit and stops the link.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the new duplex fiber patch shows no link on either switch
a light meter at the far end finds light on the wrong strand of the pair
the transceivers and the fiber type match
the cable was cut and terminated on site

answer.cause: transmit and receive strands transposed on the fiber patch
answer.action: Reverse the two strands at one end so transmit connects to receive

firstStep: Check which strand carries light with a visual fault locator or light meter
appliesWhen: the transmit of one end does not reach the receive of the other
explanation: A fiber link needs each transmit port connected to the far receive port. When the strands are reversed, both ends send light that no receiver sees.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the link came up with errors after the patch cords were moved during a rack change
the receive power on the port is several dB lower than last month
an inspection scope shows specks on the ferrule end face
the dust caps were left off the ports for a day

answer.cause: dirty fiber connectors blocking part of the light
answer.action: Clean the connector end faces and inspect them before reconnecting

firstStep: Inspect the connector end faces with a fiber scope
appliesWhen: dust or residue on the fiber end faces blocks the light
explanation: Dust or oil on a ferrule scatters light and adds loss at the connector. Cleaning the end faces restores the receive power.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the input error counter on one access port climbs every minute
the frames fail their checksum at the switch
the user on that port says file copies are slow
other ports on the same switch show no errors

answer.cause: a damaged cable or connector corrupting frames on that port
answer.action: Test the cable on that port and replace it if it fails

firstStep: Look at the interface counters with a show interface command
appliesWhen: frames arrive corrupted because of a bad cable, connector, or noise on one link
explanation: A CRC error means the frame's checksum did not match its data, so the bits were damaged on the wire. One port with rising CRC counts points to that link's cabling.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the switch port counts runts and late collisions
the server NIC was set by hand to 100 Mbps full
the switch port is left on auto
throughput drops badly under load

answer.cause: a duplex mismatch between the switch port and the server NIC
answer.action: Set both ends to the same speed and duplex, or both to auto

firstStep: Compare the speed and duplex on the switch port and the NIC
appliesWhen: one end of the link runs half duplex and the other full duplex
explanation: When one side is set by hand and the other is on auto, the auto side falls back to half duplex. The half-duplex side sees collisions and cut-off frames.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the storage server was set to send 9000-byte frames
the switch port counts giants and drops them
small pings work but large file transfers stall
the other storage servers on the switch work normally

answer.cause: jumbo frames on the server that the switch port does not accept
answer.action: Set the same MTU on the server and the switch port

firstStep: Compare the MTU settings on the server and the switch port
appliesWhen: one end sends frames larger than the other end accepts
explanation: A giant is a frame larger than the port allows. When the server sends jumbo frames and the switch port is set for 1500 bytes, the large frames are dropped.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the output discard counter on the uplink rises every night
the counts climb during the backup window
the uplink shows no CRC errors, runts, or giants
users on the floor report slow access only while backups run

answer.cause: an oversubscribed uplink whose output buffers overflow
answer.action: Add uplink capacity, such as a faster or aggregated link, or apply QoS

firstStep: Check the uplink utilization during the backup window
appliesWhen: more traffic is sent to a port than it can forward, so its buffers overflow
explanation: Drops with no error counters mean the frames were good but the port could not forward them in time. The buffers fill when traffic is more than the link can carry.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: a user plugged a small desk switch into the wall jack to add a printer
the port light on the access switch turned amber and then went dark
the switch log shows a port security violation
the port stays down after the desk switch is removed

answer.cause: a port shut down in the error-disabled state by port security
answer.action: Remove the extra device, then reset the port (shutdown, then no shutdown) or let errdisable recovery restore it

firstStep: Check the port status and the switch log
appliesWhen: the switch shut the port itself after a security or error condition
explanation: Port security puts a port in the error-disabled state when it sees more MAC addresses than allowed. The port stays down until it is reset or recovered.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the port light is off and the switch counts no errors on it
the configuration has a shutdown line under that interface
a technician worked on the switch during last night's maintenance
the cable and the PC test good

answer.cause: an interface that was disabled in the switch configuration
answer.action: Enable the interface with the no shutdown command

firstStep: Check the interface status on the switch
appliesWhen: an administrator disabled the interface in the configuration
explanation: Administratively down means someone turned the port off with a command, for example during maintenance. It stays off until it is enabled again.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: two ports were bundled into one link to the server switch
one member port shows suspended while the other forwards
the suspended port was set to 1 Gbps while its partner runs at 10 Gbps
the bundle carries only half its expected bandwidth

answer.cause: a port-channel member whose settings do not match the rest of the bundle
answer.action: Match the member port's speed, duplex, and LACP settings to the bundle

firstStep: Compare the member port settings with the other ports in the bundle
appliesWhen: a member link of a port channel has settings that differ from the others
explanation: A switch suspends a port-channel member when its settings do not match the bundle or the far end. The other members keep forwarding, so the bundle runs with less capacity.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: twelve new cameras were added to a switch that already powers the phones
the last ports connected get no power while the earlier ones work
the switch log shows power denied on several ports
each camera works when moved to a different switch

answer.cause: the switch's PoE power budget exceeded by the new devices
answer.action: Add power capacity (a bigger power supply, a second switch, or an injector) or set port power priorities

firstStep: Check the switch's PoE power use against its budget
appliesWhen: the devices together draw more power than the switch can supply
explanation: A PoE switch has a total power budget shared by all its ports. When the connected devices need more than that budget, the switch stops powering some ports.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the new access point boots but runs with only one radio
the AP's log shows it is in a low-power mode
the switch ports supply up to 15.4 W
the AP's data sheet asks for 802.3bt power

answer.cause: a switch port that supports only 802.3af PoE for a device that needs more power
answer.action: Connect the device to a PoE+ or PoE++ port, or use a matching injector

appliesWhen: the port supplies an older PoE standard than the device requires
explanation: 802.3af gives at most 15.4 W per port, while 802.3at and 802.3bt give more. A device that needs a higher standard runs in a limited mode or does not start.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: one end of the new link has a 10GBASE-SR module and the other a 10GBASE-LR module
the link does not come up
the fiber tests good with a light source and meter
each module works when paired with a module of its own type

answer.cause: mismatched transceivers that use different standards and wavelengths
answer.action: Install the same transceiver type at both ends of the link

firstStep: Read the type of the transceiver at each end
appliesWhen: the modules at the two ends use different standards or wavelengths
explanation: Both ends of a fiber link need transceivers of the same standard, data rate, and wavelength. SR modules use 850 nm and LR modules use 1310 nm, so they cannot talk to each other.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the transceiver diagnostics show receive power near the module's lowest limit
the run is long and has several splices and patch panels
the link flaps and logs errors on warm afternoons
the module types match at both ends

answer.cause: a received optical level too low for the transceiver
answer.action: Reduce the loss on the path (clean, re-splice, or remove patch points) or use longer-reach transceivers

firstStep: Read the receive power in the transceiver diagnostics (DOM)
appliesWhen: the light reaching the receiver is too weak because the path has too much loss
explanation: Each splice, connector, and meter of fiber adds loss. When the received power is close to the module's lowest limit, small changes make the link flap.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

need: choose the copper cable for drops that run through a machine shop
clues: the drops pass close to large electric motors
the runs are under 60 meters
the client devices have only RJ45 ports
appliesWhen: a short copper run must pass through strong electrical noise
explanation: Shielded twisted pair has a foil or braid that protects the pairs from outside electrical noise. It keeps the RJ45 connection that the devices need.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

need: link two buildings that are 8 kilometers apart
clues: the link must run at 10 Gbps
the path is far beyond any copper limit
the cable will run underground between the sites
appliesWhen: a high-speed link must cover several kilometers
explanation: Single-mode fiber carries light over many kilometers with little loss. Multimode and copper cannot reach that far.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

need: connect the switches in two rows of the same data center at 10 Gbps
clues: the run is about 200 meters
the budget calls for the lower-cost optics
the switches have SFP+ slots
appliesWhen: a fast link of a few hundred meters must use the lower-cost optics
explanation: Multimode fiber with SR optics covers a few hundred meters at 10 Gbps at a lower cost than single-mode. It fits links inside one building.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

need: cable new desks for 10 Gbps copper connections
clues: the longest run is 90 meters
the NICs use RJ45 ports
the building has no unusual electrical noise
appliesWhen: a copper run up to 100 meters must carry 10 Gbps
explanation: Cat 6a supports 10GBASE-T to the full 100 meters. Cat 5e and Cat 6 cannot carry 10 Gbps that far.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

need: power new pan-tilt-zoom cameras with heaters over the network cable
clues: each camera draws about 60 W
no power outlets are near the camera mounts
the current switch gives at most 30 W per port
appliesWhen: a powered device needs more than 30 W over the network cable
explanation: 802.3bt delivers 60 W or more per port, while 802.3at stops at 30 W. A high-power camera needs the newer standard.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 5: Cabling Solutions and Issues

clues: the whole floor lost the network a few minutes after a desk was moved
both ends of one patch cord are plugged into two wall jacks
the switch CPU is at 100 percent and every port light blinks fast
the switch log shows MAC addresses flapping between ports

answer.cause: a network loop on switch ports where spanning tree is turned off
answer.action: Remove the extra cable, then enable STP with BPDU guard on the access ports

firstStep: Look for a cable that connects two switch ports together
appliesWhen: two switch ports are joined by a redundant path that nothing blocks
explanation: A loop forwards broadcasts around and around because Ethernet frames have no TTL, so a broadcast storm fills every link. Spanning tree blocks redundant paths to stop this.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: traffic between two buildings now crosses an old access switch
all switches still use the default bridge priority
the old access switch has the lowest MAC address on the network
the problem started after that switch was reconnected

answer.cause: an old access switch elected as the STP root bridge
answer.action: Set a lower bridge priority on the core switch so it becomes the root

firstStep: Check which switch is the root bridge with the spanning tree show command
appliesWhen: a switch other than the core won the root bridge election
explanation: With equal priorities, the switch with the lowest MAC address becomes the root bridge. All paths are built toward the root, so a weak access switch as root sends traffic the long way.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PCs get an APIPA address after a cold boot
a manual renew a minute later gets a normal address
the switch port lights stay amber for about 30 seconds after the PC starts
the problem started after a new managed switch was installed

answer.cause: access ports that wait in the STP listening and learning states before they forward
answer.action: Enable PortFast (edge port) on the access ports

firstStep: Watch the port state on the switch while the PC boots
appliesWhen: an access port spends its first 30 seconds or so in the STP listening and learning states
explanation: A standard STP port listens and learns for about 30 seconds before it forwards. A fast-booting PC sends its DHCP request in that time and gets no reply.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: the second uplink to the core shows no traffic
the switch lists that port with the alternate role
the first uplink is up and forwarding
the manager wants both uplinks to carry traffic

answer.cause: spanning tree blocking the redundant uplink as designed
answer.action: Bundle the two uplinks into one port channel (link aggregation)

appliesWhen: STP holds a redundant link in the blocking state to prevent a loop
explanation: STP leaves one path forwarding and blocks the others, so a second uplink waits as an alternate port. A port channel makes the two links one logical link, so both carry traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: the user moved to a new desk yesterday
the PC now gets an address from the guest subnet
the user can browse the internet but cannot reach the department file server
users at nearby desks have no problems

answer.cause: the switch port at the new desk assigned to the wrong VLAN
answer.action: Assign the switch port to the user's department VLAN

firstStep: Check the VLAN that the switch port is assigned to
appliesWhen: a switch port is a member of a different VLAN than the user needs
explanation: Each VLAN is its own subnet, so the PC gets an address from whatever VLAN its port is in. A port in the guest VLAN cannot reach the department servers.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: a new VLAN for the phones works on the core switch
phones on the access switch in the second closet get no address
the other VLANs on that access switch work
the new VLAN exists on both switches

answer.cause: the new VLAN not allowed on the trunk between the switches
answer.action: Add the VLAN to the allowed list on the trunk ports at both ends

firstStep: Check the allowed VLAN list on the trunk
appliesWhen: a trunk does not carry one of the VLANs it needs
explanation: A trunk carries only the VLANs in its allowed list. If the new VLAN is left off, frames for it never reach the far switch, so its clients cannot reach the DHCP server.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: users can ping the application server
the web application times out on its custom port
a security change was applied to the router interface last night
the hit counter on the last line of the list is rising

answer.cause: an access control list that blocks the application's port
answer.action: Add a permit entry for the application's port above the deny entries

firstStep: Review the ACL entries and hit counts on the interface
appliesWhen: a filter on a router or switch interface drops the traffic
explanation: An ACL is read from the top down and ends with an implicit deny. If no permit line matches the application's port, the traffic is dropped while ping still works.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: users can reach every internal subnet
no one can reach any internet site
a traceroute stops at the router
the router was replaced yesterday and its configuration was rebuilt by hand

answer.cause: a missing default route on the edge router
answer.action: Add a default route (0.0.0.0/0) that points to the ISP's next hop

firstStep: Display the routing table on the router
appliesWhen: the router has no gateway of last resort for unknown networks
explanation: Without a default route, the router drops traffic for networks that are not in its table. Internal routes still work, so only the internet fails.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: a new subnet was added at the branch office
branch users on the new subnet can reach the internet
the head office cannot reach the new subnet
the older subnets at the branch work from the head office

answer.cause: no entry for the new subnet in the head office router's routing table
answer.action: Add a static route for the subnet, or advertise it in the routing protocol

firstStep: Display the routing table on the head office router
appliesWhen: the router has no route to one destination network
explanation: A router forwards only to networks in its routing table. The new subnet was never added or advertised, so the head office has no path to it.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: a traceroute alternates between the same two router addresses
the trace ends with TTL expired in transit
both routers have static routes added by hand last week
other destinations work normally

answer.cause: a routing loop between two routers whose static routes point at each other
answer.action: Correct the static routes so each router has the right next hop

firstStep: Run a traceroute to the destination
appliesWhen: two routers each send the traffic to the other
explanation: When router A sends a network to router B and B sends it back to A, the packet bounces until its TTL reaches zero. Fixing the conflicting routes ends the loop.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: traffic to one branch takes the slow backup VPN although the main circuit is up
the routing protocol learns the branch as part of a larger summary
the routing table also lists a /24 entry for that branch from an old test
other branches use the main circuit

answer.cause: a leftover more-specific static route that wins over the dynamic route
answer.action: Remove the leftover static route

firstStep: Look up the route for the branch in the routing table
appliesWhen: a more specific route in the table sends the traffic the wrong way
explanation: A router picks the longest matching prefix first. An old /24 static route beats the larger summary that the routing protocol learned, so traffic follows the old path.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: guests who arrived early in the day connect normally
later arrivals get a 169.254 address
the scope has 50 addresses and an 8-day lease
the DHCP server is running and answers other subnets

answer.cause: an exhausted DHCP address pool
answer.action: Enlarge the scope or shorten the lease time

firstStep: Check how many addresses in the scope are leased
appliesWhen: every address in the DHCP scope is already leased
explanation: When every address in the scope is leased, new clients get no offer and fall back to APIPA. A larger scope or shorter leases free addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: every PC on the new VLAN gets a 169.254 address
the DHCP server is on a different subnet
the new scope on the server has plenty of free addresses
a PC with a static address on the new VLAN works

answer.cause: no DHCP relay (IP helper) on the router interface for the new VLAN
answer.action: Configure a DHCP relay (IP helper address) on the VLAN's router interface

firstStep: Check the router interface for the VLAN for a helper address
appliesWhen: the DHCP requests from a subnet never reach the server on another subnet
explanation: DHCP discovers are broadcasts, and routers do not forward broadcasts. A relay on the VLAN interface forwards them to the server.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: some PCs get addresses in 192.168.0.0/24 while the LAN uses 10.10.0.0/16
those PCs have a gateway that no one recognizes
a consumer wireless router was seen under a desk
the PCs that renew later may get a correct address

answer.cause: an unauthorized DHCP server handing out leases
answer.action: Remove the device and enable DHCP snooping on the switches

firstStep: Run ipconfig /all on an affected PC to see which DHCP server gave the lease
appliesWhen: a second, unapproved DHCP server answers clients
explanation: Clients take the first DHCP offer they hear. A consumer router answering requests gives out its own range and gateway.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC can reach the printer and the file server on its own subnet
it cannot reach any other subnet or the internet
ipconfig shows the gateway as 10.1.1.254 while the router interface is 10.1.1.1
the PC has a static address set by hand

answer.cause: an incorrect default gateway on the PC
answer.action: Set the default gateway to the router's address

firstStep: Compare the gateway in ipconfig with the router's interface address
appliesWhen: a host points to the wrong address to leave its subnet
explanation: A host sends traffic for other subnets to its default gateway. When that address is not the router, local traffic works but nothing leaves the subnet.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: all DHCP clients on one subnet reach only local hosts
the computers with static settings on the same subnet work
the DHCP scope was edited yesterday
the clients show a router option of 10.2.0.10, which is a printer

answer.cause: a wrong router option in the DHCP scope
answer.action: Correct the router (default gateway) option in the scope and have the clients renew

firstStep: Check the router option in the DHCP scope
appliesWhen: the DHCP scope gives every client the wrong gateway
explanation: DHCP gives each client its gateway from the scope's router option. A wrong value sends every DHCP client to a host that does not route.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC shows an address conflict message
a network printer and a PC lose their connections in turn
the printer was given a static address inside the DHCP range
arp -a shows two different MAC addresses for the same address over time

answer.cause: two devices using the same IP address
answer.action: Give the printer an address outside the DHCP range, or a DHCP reservation

firstStep: Check the ARP table for the MAC address that answers that address
appliesWhen: two hosts have the same address
explanation: Every address on a network must be unique. A static address inside the DHCP range can be leased to another device, so the two take turns losing traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC was moved from the head office to the branch
it still has the static address it used at the head office
it cannot reach anything, even the branch printer
other PCs at the branch use DHCP and work

answer.cause: a static IP address from another subnet
answer.action: Set an address from the local subnet, or switch the PC to DHCP

firstStep: Compare the PC's address with the addresses used at the branch
appliesWhen: a host has an address that belongs to a different network
explanation: A host can only talk directly to hosts in its own subnet and needs a gateway on that subnet. An address from the old site leaves it with no local neighbors and no gateway it can reach.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC has address 10.1.5.20 with mask 255.255.0.0
the LAN is 10.1.5.0/24
it cannot reach servers on 10.1.8.0/24 but can reach internet sites
the gateway and DNS settings are correct

answer.cause: an incorrect subnet mask that is too wide
answer.action: Set the subnet mask to 255.255.255.0

firstStep: Compare the PC's mask with the mask of the subnet
appliesWhen: a host's mask makes it think remote hosts are on its own subnet
explanation: With a /16 mask the PC treats 10.1.8.x as local and sends ARP requests that no one answers, instead of using the gateway. Internet traffic still goes to the gateway, so it works.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC has address 192.168.10.20 with mask 255.255.255.192
the LAN is 192.168.10.0/24 and the router is 192.168.10.1
it cannot reach the file server at 192.168.10.200 on the same switch
it can reach the PCs at addresses 192.168.10.2 to .62

answer.cause: a subnet mask that is too narrow for the LAN
answer.action: Set the subnet mask to 255.255.255.0

firstStep: Compare the PC's mask with the mask of the subnet
appliesWhen: a host's mask makes it think local hosts are on another subnet
explanation: With a /26 mask the PC sees only .1 to .62 as local. It sends traffic for .200 to the gateway, and other hosts outside its small range seem unreachable.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: stop users' desk switches from causing problems in the spanning tree
clues: users sometimes plug small switches into wall jacks
an access port must shut down if it hears switch control messages
end devices on these ports never send BPDUs

answer.item: BPDU guard on the access ports

appliesWhen: an access port must shut down when another switch is connected to it
explanation: BPDU guard error-disables an access port when a BPDU arrives on it. End devices never send BPDUs, so only a connected switch triggers it.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: make sure the core switch is always the center of the spanning tree
clues: all switches use the default settings
older access switches have lower MAC addresses than the core
the change must be made on the core switch

answer.item: A lower bridge priority on the core switch

appliesWhen: one chosen switch must always win the root bridge election
explanation: The root bridge is the switch with the lowest bridge ID, which is the priority followed by the MAC address. A lower priority makes the core win no matter its MAC address.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: keep a partner's switch from taking over the spanning tree
clues: the partner's switch connects to a downlink port and must still pass traffic
the port must keep working while the partner's switch accepts the current root
a superior BPDU from that side must not change the topology

answer.item: Root guard on the downlink port

appliesWhen: a downlink must stay up but never lead to a new root bridge
explanation: Root guard blocks a port only while it receives superior BPDUs that would move the root. The downstream switch can keep its link as long as it accepts the current root.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: let PCs start using the network as soon as their ports come up
clues: the PCs are on single access ports with no other switches
the ports take about 30 seconds to pass traffic
the PCs sometimes miss their DHCP lease at boot

answer.item: PortFast (edge port) on the access ports

appliesWhen: an access port must skip the STP listening and learning delay
explanation: PortFast moves an edge port straight to forwarding, so a booting PC can reach DHCP at once. It belongs only on ports with end devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: make sure clients get leases only from the approved server
clues: a consumer router once gave out leases on the LAN
the approved server is reached through the uplink port
the switches are managed

answer.item: DHCP snooping with the uplink port set as trusted

appliesWhen: only DHCP offers from a trusted port must reach the clients
explanation: DHCP snooping drops DHCP server messages that arrive on untrusted ports. Only the uplink to the approved server is trusted, so a rogue server's offers are dropped.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: file copies crawl every weekday from ten to eleven in the morning
the uplink graph shows close to 100 percent use in that hour
a nightly job was recently moved to run in the morning
transfers are fast again by late morning

answer.cause: congestion from a large backup job that fills the link during business hours
answer.action: Reschedule the backup job to run outside business hours

appliesWhen: one heavy job fills a link at a set time of day
explanation: The slowdown matches the hour when the link is full, and it began when a large job moved into that hour. Moving the job out of business hours removes the congestion.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting
firstStep: Check the link utilization graph for the slow period

clues: the computers in one lab slow down as more students log on
the lab device has link lights that all blink together
the collision counters on the lab NICs keep rising
the computers in other rooms are fast

answer.cause: contention on a shared hub, where every device competes for one collision domain
answer.action: Replace the hub with a switch

appliesWhen: many devices share one collision domain and wait for each other to send
explanation: A hub repeats every frame to every port, so all the lab computers compete for the same medium and collide. A switch gives each port its own collision domain.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: each server has a 10 Gbps NIC
the access switch connects to the core over a single 1 Gbps port
servers on the same switch talk to each other at full speed
traffic to the core never goes above about 1 Gbps

answer.cause: a bottleneck at the slow uplink between the access switch and the core
answer.action: Upgrade the uplink to 10 Gbps or aggregate several uplinks with LACP

appliesWhen: one link in the path has much less capacity than the links that feed it
explanation: Local traffic is fast while traffic through the uplink tops out at that port's speed, so the uplink limits the whole path. A faster or aggregated uplink removes the bottleneck.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting
firstStep: Compare the speed of each link in the path

clues: the office grew from 10 to 40 staff this year
the circuit runs at its full rated speed all day
the ISP confirms the line has no faults
cloud apps are slow for everyone at once

answer.cause: a WAN circuit whose bandwidth is too small for the number of users
answer.action: Upgrade the circuit to a higher bandwidth tier

appliesWhen: the circuit works as designed but its capacity is too small for the demand
explanation: The circuit has no fault and runs at its rated speed, but the demand has grown past its capacity. More throughput capacity is the fix.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: the contract is for 500 Mbps
tests from a wired PC show about 90 Mbps at every hour
only one person uses the connection
the router's own LAN ports test at full speed

answer.cause: an ISP circuit that delivers far less throughput than the contracted bandwidth
answer.action: Contact the ISP with the test results and have them fix the circuit

appliesWhen: the measured throughput is far below what the ISP contract promises with little local use
explanation: One user on a wired PC gets a small part of the contracted rate at all hours, so local load does not explain it. The ISP must fix the circuit or its provisioning.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting
firstStep: Run a speed test from a wired computer and compare it with the contract

clues: the remote site's only internet link is a geostationary service
round-trip times are about 600 ms
large downloads reach their full rate after a while
two-way calls have long pauses between speakers

answer.cause: high latency from the long path to a geostationary satellite
answer.action: Move interactive traffic to a terrestrial or low-orbit link

appliesWhen: the signal travels a very long distance, so every round trip takes a long time
explanation: A geostationary orbit is far from the earth, so each round trip takes about half a second even when the link has bandwidth to spare. Interactive traffic needs a shorter path.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: remote staff connect through the company tunnel
all traffic goes to a concentrator on another continent
a trace to a nearby website crosses an ocean twice
video meetings lag only while the tunnel is up

answer.cause: high latency because a full tunnel sends all internet traffic through a distant concentrator
answer.action: Use split tunneling or a closer VPN gateway for internet traffic

appliesWhen: traffic takes a long detour through a far-away gateway before it reaches nearby services
explanation: With the tunnel up, even nearby sites are reached through a far-away concentrator, which adds a long round trip. Split tunneling or a closer gateway shortens the path.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: a continuous test to the server drops about 5 percent of replies
the switch port shows rising input errors and FCS errors
the patch cord was crushed under a desk wheel
other ports on the switch have no errors

answer.cause: a damaged patch cable that corrupts frames so the switch drops them
answer.action: Replace the damaged patch cable

appliesWhen: a damaged cable corrupts frames so the receiver discards them
explanation: Frames that fail the checksum are dropped, and only this port has rising errors on a crushed cord. A new cable stops the corrupted frames.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting
firstStep: Check the interface counters on the switch port

clues: one end of the link is set by hand and the other auto-negotiates
the switch port reports late collisions
pings work but file copies are very slow
the problem started after the port was set to 100 Mbps by hand

answer.cause: a duplex mismatch between the switch port and the server NIC
answer.action: Set both ends of the link to the same speed and duplex, or both to auto-negotiate

appliesWhen: one end of a link runs full duplex and the other runs half duplex
explanation: When one side is set by hand, the other side may fall back to half duplex. Late collisions and slow transfers are the sign of that mismatch.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting
firstStep: Compare the speed and duplex settings on both ends of the link

clues: callers sound choppy and robotic
the average delay is low but it changes from 5 ms to 90 ms
the problem is worst while large files are copied
all traffic is in one queue on the router

answer.cause: jitter because voice packets wait in the same queue as bulk data
answer.action: Configure QoS so voice traffic is marked and sent first

appliesWhen: the delay of real-time packets changes a lot because they share a queue with bulk data
explanation: Voice needs packets to arrive at an even pace. With one shared queue, bulk data makes the delay change from packet to packet, which breaks up the audio.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: three nearby APs use 2.4 GHz channels 3, 4, and 8
throughput drops when all three APs are busy
the signal strength looks good everywhere
a scan shows many retries on each AP

answer.cause: co-channel and adjacent-channel interference from overlapping 2.4 GHz channels
answer.action: Set the 2.4 GHz APs to channels 1, 6, and 11

appliesWhen: nearby APs use 2.4 GHz channels that are too close together
explanation: In the 2.4 GHz band, only channels 1, 6, and 11 do not overlap. APs on channels in between spill into each other, which causes retries and low throughput.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting; CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
firstStep: Run a Wi-Fi scan to see which channels the nearby APs use

clues: laptops near the break room lose connection around lunchtime
the drops last a minute or two at a time
the laptops use the 2.4 GHz band
devices on 5 GHz in the same room have no problem

answer.cause: RF interference from a microwave oven that works in the 2.4 GHz band
answer.action: Move the clients to the 5 GHz band or move the AP away from the break room

appliesWhen: a nearby appliance sends noise in the 2.4 GHz band for short periods
explanation: A microwave oven leaks energy at about 2.4 GHz, so drops near the break room at meal times point to it. The 5 GHz band avoids that noise.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting; CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking

clues: users in the records room get a weak signal
the room is 10 meters from the AP behind a concrete wall and metal shelves
the open area at the same distance from the AP has a strong signal
the RSSI in the room is close to -80 dBm

answer.cause: signal attenuation from the concrete wall and metal shelves between the AP and the room
answer.action: Add an AP inside the room or move the AP so the signal does not pass through the wall

appliesWhen: dense materials such as concrete or metal absorb or reflect the signal between the AP and the clients
explanation: The open area at the same distance has a good signal, so distance is not the problem. Concrete and metal absorb and reflect RF, which weakens the signal in that room.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting; CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
firstStep: Measure the RSSI inside the room and in the open area

clues: a new wing opened last month
the nearest AP is at the far end of the old building
devices in the new wing show one bar or no network at all
the heat map from the original survey stops at the old wall

answer.cause: insufficient wireless coverage because no AP serves the new wing
answer.action: Do a new site survey and install APs in the new wing

appliesWhen: an area is too far from any AP to get a usable signal
explanation: The wing was added after the original survey, and the closest AP is too far away. A new survey shows where to place APs to cover it.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting; CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking

clues: all APs are set to their maximum output
laptops stay connected to an AP two rooms away
phones show a strong signal but uploads are slow
the cells of nearby APs overlap a lot on the heat map

answer.cause: AP transmit power set too high, so cells overlap and clients stay on distant APs
answer.action: Lower the AP transmit power so each AP covers only its own area

appliesWhen: APs transmit so strongly that their cells overlap and clients join APs that are too far away
explanation: A client hears a loud AP from far away and stays on it, but its own weaker signal back to that AP gives poor uploads. Lower power makes clients use the closest AP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking

clues: many clients drop from the network at the same moment
the controller log shows a flood of management frames from one MAC address
the clients reconnect and drop again within seconds
a new network with a similar name appeared nearby

answer.cause: a deauthentication attack that forces clients off the AP, possibly to push them to an evil twin
answer.action: Enable 802.11w protected management frames and locate the rogue transmitter

appliesWhen: an attacker sends forged frames that force clients to leave the AP
explanation: Forged management frames make clients leave the real AP all at once, and a look-alike network suggests an evil twin. Protected management frames reject forged frames.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

clues: laptops lose the network when users walk from the first to the second floor
the second-floor AP was replaced last week
users must pick the network and type the key again upstairs
the signal is strong on both floors

answer.cause: a replaced AP whose SSID or security settings do not match the other APs
answer.action: Configure the new AP with the same SSID and security settings as the other APs

appliesWhen: the APs do not all use the same SSID and security settings, so clients cannot move between them
explanation: Clients move between APs only when the APs share the same SSID and security settings. Having to join again on the new AP's floor shows that its settings differ.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking

clues: handheld scanners switch APs many times a minute while users stand still
each switch causes a short pause in the app
the APs share the same network name and key
the change rule was edited on the controller last week

answer.cause: a roaming threshold set so that clients hand over between APs too often
answer.action: Adjust the roaming threshold on the controller to a sensible signal level

appliesWhen: the signal level that triggers a handover is set wrong, so clients change APs too often or too late
explanation: The APs match, but the devices change APs even when they do not move, so the handover trigger is wrong. A better threshold stops the needless handovers.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: check whether a workstation can reach its default gateway
clues: the user says nothing on the network works
the technician is at a Windows command prompt
only a quick yes-or-no reachability test is needed
appliesWhen: a quick ICMP echo test shows whether one host can reach another
explanation: ping sends ICMP echo requests and reports each reply and its round-trip time. A reply from the gateway shows the local link and addressing work.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: find where along the path traffic to a remote server slows down or stops
clues: the server is several routers away
the technician wants a list of each hop and its delay
the user is on a Windows workstation
appliesWhen: the path to a remote host must be listed hop by hop with the delay at each router
explanation: tracert sends packets with a rising TTL, so each router on the path answers in turn. The hop where the delay jumps or the replies stop shows where the problem is.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: check which IP address the company DNS server returns for an intranet name
clues: users reach the site by IP address but not by name
the workstation runs Windows
the technician wants to query the name server directly
appliesWhen: a name must be checked against a DNS server from a Windows command prompt
explanation: nslookup sends a query to a DNS server and shows the server used and the address it returns. A wrong or empty answer points to a DNS problem.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: see the full answer and authority sections for the mail exchanger records of a domain
clues: the technician is in a Linux shell
the output must show the TTL and flags of each record
the query should go to one specific name server
appliesWhen: detailed DNS records must be queried from a Linux or macOS shell
explanation: dig is the Linux and macOS DNS lookup tool, and it prints each section of the reply with TTLs and flags. It can ask a chosen server for one record type such as MX.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: list the ports a server is listening on and its active connections
clues: a service may not have started on the server
the check must be done on the server itself
the technician also wants to see which remote hosts are connected
appliesWhen: a host's own listening ports and active connections must be listed
explanation: netstat shows the local host's TCP and UDP connections and listening ports, and netstat -a lists them all. It confirms whether the service is listening.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: see the IP address, gateway, DNS servers, and lease details of a Windows laptop
clues: the laptop may have an address in the 169.254.0.0/16 range
the technician also wants to release and renew the lease
the laptop runs Windows
appliesWhen: a Windows host's own IP settings and lease must be shown or renewed
explanation: ipconfig /all shows the address, mask, gateway, DNS servers, and DHCP lease on Windows. ipconfig /release and /renew request a new lease.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: view the interfaces and IPv4 addresses of a modern Linux server
clues: the server runs a current Linux release
the old net-tools package is not installed
the technician wants to see the state of each interface
appliesWhen: a Linux host's interface settings must be shown with the current tool
explanation: On current Linux releases, ip replaces ifconfig, and ip address show lists each interface with its state and addresses. ifconfig needs the older net-tools package.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: see which hardware address a workstation has stored for the gateway's IP address
clues: two devices may be using the same IP address
the check is done on the user's Windows workstation
the technician wants the local IP-to-MAC cache
appliesWhen: the IP-to-MAC mappings that a host has cached must be shown
explanation: arp -a lists the host's cache of IP addresses and their MAC addresses. If the gateway's entry changes between MAC addresses, two devices claim that address.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: capture the packets on an interface of a Linux server that has no desktop
clues: only an SSH session to the server is available
the capture must be saved to a file for later study
a filter must keep only traffic on port 443
appliesWhen: packets must be captured from the command line of a Linux or Unix host
explanation: tcpdump captures packets from the command line with filters and can write them to a pcap file. The file can later be opened in a protocol analyzer.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: decode a capture to see why a web app's TCP sessions keep resetting
clues: the capture file is already saved
the technician wants each packet's headers shown in readable form
the work is done on a Windows desktop with a graphical tool

answer.item: A protocol analyzer such as Wireshark

appliesWhen: captured traffic must be decoded and read protocol by protocol
explanation: A protocol analyzer reads and decodes the captured frames, so the technician can see each header, flag, and retransmission. It shows where the resets come from.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: find every host on a subnet and the services each one offers
clues: the scan runs from one admin laptop
the results must list open TCP ports and service versions
the change was approved by the security team
appliesWhen: remote hosts must be discovered and their open ports listed from across the network
explanation: Nmap is a port scanner that discovers live hosts and the open ports and services on each one. netstat shows only the local host.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: learn which switch and port a VoIP phone is plugged into
clues: the switches and phones come from three vendors
the cables are not labeled
the devices advertise their neighbors at Layer 2
appliesWhen: devices from many vendors must report their directly connected neighbors
explanation: LLDP is the vendor-neutral Layer 2 discovery protocol, so the switch can show the phone's name, port, and capabilities. CDP works only between Cisco devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: see the model and interface of each device connected to a router
clues: every router and switch in the network is from Cisco
the vendor's own protocol is enabled by default
the admin is at the router's console
appliesWhen: an all-Cisco network must report directly connected neighbor devices
explanation: CDP is Cisco's own Layer 2 discovery protocol and is on by default on Cisco devices. show cdp neighbors lists each connected device and port.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: confirm whether the internet connection delivers the rate in the ISP contract
clues: the users say the connection seems slow
the test should run from a wired computer
the result must show download and upload rates in Mbps
appliesWhen: the real download and upload rates of a connection must be compared with the contract
explanation: A speed tester measures the actual download and upload throughput to a test server. The result can be compared with the contracted bandwidth.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: find which unlabeled patch panel port connects to a wall jack
clues: the wall jack is in a room on another floor
dozens of cables end in the wiring closet
the technician can put a device on the jack and listen in the closet
appliesWhen: one unlabeled cable must be traced from one end to the other
explanation: The tone generator puts a signal on the cable at the jack, and the probe sounds when it touches that cable in the closet. This traces one cable among many.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: check that a newly terminated Cat 6 cable has every pair wired correctly
clues: the technician crimped both ends by hand
the result must show opens, shorts, and crossed pairs
the cable is copper twisted pair
appliesWhen: the wiring of a copper cable must be checked for opens, shorts, and miswires
explanation: A cable tester sends a signal down each pair and shows whether each pin reaches the right pin at the far end. It finds opens, shorts, and crossed pairs.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: copy all traffic on a busy link to a monitoring system without dropping frames
clues: a switch mirror port dropped frames under heavy load
the device must be passive and add no point of failure
the monitor needs both directions of the link
appliesWhen: an exact passive copy of all traffic on a link must go to a monitor
explanation: A tap sits inline and passively copies every frame in both directions to the monitor. It does not drop frames under load the way a mirror port can.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: choose the least crowded channel for a new access point
clues: several nearby businesses run their own wireless networks
the tool should show the signal level of each network in dBm
the technician carries a laptop through the area
appliesWhen: the channels and signal levels of nearby wireless networks must be measured
explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer lists nearby networks with their channels and signal levels. The technician can then pick the clearest channel.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting; CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking

need: find the exact spot of a break or tight bend in a short fiber patch cord
clues: the link light is off on a fiber uplink
the cord is only a few meters long
the technician wants to see the fault with the eye
appliesWhen: a break or bend in a short fiber run must be seen directly
explanation: A visual fault locator sends bright red laser light into the fiber, and the light shows through the jacket at a break or tight bend. It finds faults in short runs.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: find which switch port a laptop with a known hardware address is connected to
clues: the admin knows the laptop's hardware address
the admin is logged in to the access switch
the switch learns the source address of each frame on each port
appliesWhen: the switch port where a device's hardware address was learned must be found
explanation: The switch keeps a table of each learned MAC address with its port and VLAN. Looking up the laptop's address in it gives the port.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: check whether a router has a path to a remote subnet
clues: users cannot reach one remote subnet
the admin is at the router's command line
the router learns paths from OSPF and has a few static entries
appliesWhen: the paths that a router knows to each network must be checked
explanation: show route (show ip route on Cisco) lists the networks the router knows, the next hop, and how each was learned. A missing entry explains the unreachable subnet.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: check one switch port for errors, duplex, and speed
clues: a server on that port has slow transfers
the admin wants the input error and CRC counters
the admin is logged in to the switch
appliesWhen: the status, speed, duplex, and error counters of a port must be checked
explanation: show interface shows a port's state, speed, duplex, and counters such as CRC errors and collisions. Rising errors point to a cable or duplex problem.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: review the settings that a router is running after a change
clues: a colleague changed the router last night
the admin wants to read every setting that is active now
the admin will compare the output with the saved backup
appliesWhen: the full set of settings on a device must be reviewed
explanation: show config (show running-config on Cisco) prints the device's current configuration. Comparing it with the backup shows what changed.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: see which hardware address the router has stored for a server's IP address
clues: the check must be done on the router, not on a host
a server was replaced but kept its old IP address
the admin wants the router's IP-to-MAC entries
appliesWhen: a router's own IP-to-MAC mappings must be shown
explanation: show arp lists the router's ARP cache of IP addresses and MAC addresses. An old MAC for the replaced server shows a stale entry.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: confirm which ports on a switch belong to the guest network segment
clues: a guest laptop got an address from the staff range
the switch has several Layer 2 segments
the admin wants the ports listed by segment
appliesWhen: the ports assigned to each VLAN on a switch must be listed
explanation: show vlan lists each VLAN with its name and the ports assigned to it. A guest port in the staff VLAN explains the wrong address.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting

need: find out why new IP phones on one switch do not power on
clues: the phones get their power from the switch ports
ten more phones were added this week
the admin wants the power budget that is used and left
appliesWhen: the PoE budget and the power drawn on each port must be checked
explanation: show power shows the switch's PoE budget, the power in use, and the power on each port. A used-up budget means new phones get no power.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 10: Network Troubleshooting
